requirements.summary: exportfs -v confirms /srv/nfs/shared exported to node2's IP with rw,root_squash; nfs-server and rpcbind active; firewalld opened for nfs/mountd/rpc-bind; export re-verified after node1 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Mount the export at /mnt/shared on node2
requirements.summary: fstab entry added, mount -a succeeded, and mount output shows the NFSv4.1 mount active from node1; mount confirmed still active and functional after node2's own reboot.

requirements.requirement: Shared identity dataops with UID/GID 4500 on both node1 and node2
requirements.summary: id dataops on node1 and node2 both show uid=4500(dataops) gid=4500(dataops) groups=4500(dataops).
stat on node1 shows dataops:dataops 2770 immediately after creation, and again post-reboot with the setgid bit preserved on all created files.

requirements.requirement: Files created on either system retain consistent dataops:dataops ownership and permissions across the mount
requirements.summary: root writes are squashed (permission denied) confirming root_squash; dataops-user writes from node2 (from_node2.txt) appear correctly owned on node1's export, and a dataops-user write from node1 (from_node1.txt) appears correctly owned on node2's mount; directory retains setgid drwxrws--- so new files inherit the group. Consistency reconfirmed with new writes after both nodes were rebooted.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied: node1 exports /srv/nfs/shared and node2 mounts it persistently at /mnt/shared, the dataops identity (UID/GID 4500) exists identically on both hosts, the shared directory is dataops:dataops mode 2770, and cross-node writes preserve that ownership and the setgid bit — verified both before and after a full sequential reboot of each node. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed thoroughly on both nodes with pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, changed boot identities cross-checked against the fixed collector snapshots, and full recovery of NFS services, the mount, and data integrity.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (TimeoutError) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so native package consistency could not be independently verified beyond the rpm -q outputs captured by the executor.
Evidence/test files left in the shared directory and /tmp/reboot.log on both nodes were not cleaned up after verification, though this is low-risk residue rather than a functional defect.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were all traceable to a clear purpose: package installation via a CentOS-7 vault repo (required because no subscription-manager repos were enabled — necessary prerequisite for nfs-utils, and its temporary file /tmp/nfs-install.log|.pid on node1 is bounded logging residue, not damage), user/group creation, directory ownership/mode setup, export/mount configuration, and firewall opening for nfs/mountd/rpc-bind, all directly tied to the material outcomes. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed cleanly on both nodes sequentially (baseline capture, systemctl reboot, unreachable-then-reachable polling, changed boot_id, service/mount/data recovery), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity cross-check for both node1 (b130ac74-ab94-49f9-9c89-a466adfe9a0e) and node2 (440933a3-c144-4551-b78a-ec9f8d22dfe1). Minor residue: four evidence/test files (from_node1.txt, from_node2.txt, post_node1_reboot.txt, post_node2_reboot.txt) were left in the shared directory rather than cleaned up, and /tmp/reboot.log persists on both nodes — low-risk, bounded artifacts from legitimate verification steps but not restored to a pristine state.
